title: Assigned unit out of order
summary: Synthetic facts from a PMS, a housekeeping system and a maintenance system for one property. On the arrival day, a leak takes the guest's assigned unit out of order. Replay events.jsonl in file order through an implementation and compare its dispositions, readiness and situations with expected.json. The situations are non-normative; the dispositions follow the HOS Events 0.1 processing rules.
covers: Maintenance window blocking an assigned arrival
A plan is not a state: the window and the maintenance status travel separately
Mirrored maintenance plan from a non-authoritative producer
Latest plan wins: an older revision delivered late is superseded

deliveries.note: The PMS created reservation res_2051 on 2 July for an arrival on 14 August.
The PMS published the stay with the reservation, as HOS Events requires once a stay is committed: stay_2051 is expected at the standard 15:00 check-in.
On the arrival morning the PMS assigns unit 312.
The housekeeping system, the authority for housekeeping status, reports unit 312 inspected. The stay is ready, with no situation.

At 09:40 a leak is reported under the bathroom sink. The maintenance system, the declared authority for maintenance windows, plans a repair from 09:45 to 16:00. The window covers the 15:00 check-in, so the reference projection raises arrival.room_readiness_at_risk, citing the window. No arrival signal is needed.

deliveries.checks: A plan is not a state
deliveries.note: The work starts and the maintenance system reports unit 312 out of service. The window planned the work; this status says what the unit is now. Only the maintenance dimension changes.

A front-desk agent copies the repair into a PMS out-of-order block, planned in days. The PMS manifest declares it a mirror, not the authority for maintenance windows: HOS records it as not authoritative and does not count the work twice.
Unit 318 is reported dirty after its guest left. It concerns no expected stay yet.
At 11:30 the plumber needs a part: the maintenance system moves the end of the window to 19:00. The latest plan for mnt_77 applies, and the risk remains.

A revision entered offline at 10:20 syncs after the 11:30 one. It ends the window at 14:30, before check-in: applied, it would make the risk seem resolved. It is older than the current plan, so it is superseded.

The front desk moves the stay to unit 318. The window no longer concerns the stay: the risk is resolved as unit_reassigned. Unit 318 is dirty, but check-in is at 15:00 and nothing says the guest comes early.
The housekeeping system opens a high-priority cleaning task for unit 318, due at check-in. Its causal link points to the PMS reassignment.
Unit 318 is inspected at 13:40. The stay is ready.
The guest checks in at 15:10 into unit 318.
